batching.warning: Consecutive calls are an upper-bound heuristic only; they do not prove that a model decision was unnecessary between commands.

limitations: Session history size does not establish cache status or billed cost.
Unmatched, composite, truncated, malformed, and unsupported records reduce confidence.
Normalized shapes intentionally omit command arguments and exact paths.
The analyzer does not execute, replay, upload, or inspect workspace contents.
The batching-pair count is not a claim that those calls could or should be batched.

observation_token_estimate.warning: These are heuristic size estimates, not tokenizer counts and not provider-measured uncached input.

methodology.output_attribution: Only exact session/call-id matches with one non-composite observation are attributed. Batch output is never multiplied across subcommands.

terse_adapters.edge_cases: Doc tests, nextest, ignored tests, and doctest failures
terse_adapters.fallback: Retain warnings and all nonzero-exit output
terse_adapters.information_loss_risks: Hiding package-specific warnings or ignored-test context
terse_adapters.title: Cargo test successful output

terse_adapters.edge_cases: Warnings, notes, dependency errors, and machine-readable formats
terse_adapters.fallback: Preserve any diagnostic text; aggregate only clean success
terse_adapters.information_loss_risks: Dropping a warning that the next command treats as an error
terse_adapters.title: Compiler / linter output

terse_adapters.edge_cases: ANSI controls, binary matches, context groups, and truncation
terse_adapters.fallback: Byte-for-byte passthrough on parse or encoding failure
terse_adapters.information_loss_risks: Losing match context or stable result ordering
terse_adapters.title: rg / grep output

terse_adapters.edge_cases: Warnings, skips, xfails, collection errors, and plugin output
terse_adapters.fallback: Retain summaries/warnings; passthrough every failing run
terse_adapters.information_loss_risks: Removing a warning that later explains a failure
terse_adapters.title: pytest successful output

terse_adapters.edge_cases: Framework-specific reporters, snapshots, and coverage tables
terse_adapters.fallback: Keep summaries and warnings; passthrough failures
terse_adapters.information_loss_risks: Losing suite names or flaky-test warnings
terse_adapters.title: JavaScript test successful output

terse_adapters.edge_cases: Cached results, package failures, races, and multiple packages
terse_adapters.fallback: Retain one summary per package and all failures
terse_adapters.information_loss_risks: Dropping package names needed to select a retry
terse_adapters.title: Go test successful output

terse_adapters.edge_cases: Binary files, encoding errors, globs, and context-dependent source
terse_adapters.information_loss_risks: Silently omitting content the model needed to inspect
terse_adapters.title: Filesystem / source reads

terse_adapters.edge_cases: Combined diffs, binary patches, rename metadata, and truncation
terse_adapters.fallback: Passthrough; no terse transform recommended initially
terse_adapters.information_loss_risks: Deleting context required for review or patch application
terse_adapters.title: git diff

terse_adapters.edge_cases: Merge topology, rename detection, binary files, and custom formats
terse_adapters.fallback: Preserve full output unless a proven lossless formatter is selected
terse_adapters.information_loss_risks: Losing commit/stat detail needed for review
terse_adapters.title: git log / show --stat

terse_adapters.edge_cases: Branch/upstream advice, renames, conflicts, and porcelain formats
terse_adapters.fallback: Only strip control codes; otherwise preserve output
terse_adapters.title: git status

terse_adapters.edge_cases: Dependency conflicts, audit output, lifecycle scripts, and progress
terse_adapters.fallback: Preserve warnings/errors and prefer native quiet flags
terse_adapters.information_loss_risks: Hiding a security or dependency-resolution warning
terse_adapters.title: Package manager output
